licence.the_CC_line_in_the_pdf_is_a_trap: Every page of this download carries the Wiley stamp '... See the Terms and Conditions ... on Wiley Online Library for rules of use; OA articles are governed by the applicable Creative Commons License'. That clause is CONDITIONAL boilerplate printed on every Wiley PDF regardless of access status, and it does not assert that THIS article is OA. It is not a licence statement for this paper, and reading it as one would have recorded a CC licence for an All-Rights-Reserved article. The briefing for this curation did read it that way; the three records above are what settled it.
licence.section_8_verdict: FAILS CLAUDE.md section 8, which requires every constituent source to be CC0/CC-BY-compatible before corpus release. Recorded as DECISIONS.md D-1, STATUS: OPEN. Not a reason to discard the extraction -- the corpus already carries 14 CC BY-NC-ND sources recorded the same way -- but it is a release blocker the user has to rule on.
